::: {.tsk-page-lede}
Different skills solve different problems. A grounding exercise is useful when arousal is high, but it will not replace a plan for a long-term goal. This page helps you choose the job before choosing the tool.
:::

## Choosing a tool {#choosing-a-tool}

Start with three questions:

1. **How activated am I?** If the intensity is very high, begin with distress tolerance, grounding, paced breathing, or a brief mindfulness skill.
2. **Is this mainly an emotion, thought, relationship, or action problem?** Match the skill family to the part you can influence.
3. **Do I need relief, understanding, communication, or movement?** A skill should have a clear job.

## A practical sequence

### 1. Stabilize

When the nervous system is highly activated, use a short skill that reduces the chance of impulsive action. See [Distress tolerance](distress-tolerance.qmd) and [Mindfulness](mindfulness.qmd).

### 2. Understand

Once there is enough space to think, identify what is happening. Name the emotion, notice the thought, and check what the situation actually requires. See [Emotion regulation](emotion-regulation.qmd) and [CBT skills](cbt-skills.qmd).

### 3. Act effectively

Choose a behavior that moves the situation in a useful direction. That might be a request, a boundary, a five-minute task, a repair attempt, or a wellness action. See [Interpersonal effectiveness](interpersonal-effectiveness.qmd), [Goal setting](goal-setting.qmd), and [Wellness](wellness.qmd).

### 4. Widen the system

Not every useful action is problem solving. Rest, play, curiosity, and making something can restore flexibility and interest. See [Recreativity](recreativity.qmd).

::: {.tsk-note}
**Tool rule:** use the smallest skill that is likely to help with the current job. If it does not help, reassess the job instead of assuming you failed at the skill.
:::

## Skill families

| Area | Best used for | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Distress tolerance | Getting through a high-intensity moment | STOP, grounding, paced breathing |
| Mindfulness | Returning attention to what is happening now | Observe and describe, one-mindfully |
| Emotion regulation | Understanding and changing emotional responses | Check the facts, opposite action |
| CBT | Examining predictions and behavior patterns | Thought record, behavioral activation |
| Interpersonal effectiveness | Requests, boundaries, conflict, repair | DEAR MAN, GIVE, FAST |
| Goal setting | Turning direction into action | Tiny next step, implementation intentions |
| Wellness | Supporting capacity and consistency | Sleep routine, movement, basic-needs check |
| Recreativity | Reintroducing curiosity, play, and novelty | Creative reset, play window |
